groups.title: Whole labels, not logos
groups.description: Large red and black emblems, a perforated predicted label mask, and an incomplete predicted bottle mask. The complete visible paper and its text must survive.

groups.title: Label-only photographs
groups.description: Front, back, edge-cropped and tilted label close-ups. No neck or cap is required. Without an enclosing bottle detection, preserve original-frame context.

groups.title: Tap and capture reticle
groups.description: Balanced multi-bottle scenes with an explicit tap or reticle. A tap on label artwork resolves to the owning bottle. These are additional interaction capabilities, not like-for-like passive ranking cases.

groups.title: Hand association
groups.description: Off-center neck/body grips, a large hand bounding box crossing background bottles, and a hand moved clear of a bottle. Mask adjacency supports contact; box overlap alone must not establish a grip.

groups.title: Scale, edges and orientation
groups.description: An off-center foreground bottle, top truncation, a bottle crossing a side edge, and a rotated camera. Edge contact must not outweigh clear foreground intent.

groups.title: Intent despite poor readability
groups.description: A rear label, glare, low light and a body grip. The intended bottle stays the subject even when another label is easier to read. Focus contributes only weakly.

groups.title: No clear main bottle
groups.description: Two or three equal bottles, two equally held bottles, and a wide shelf row. Intent remains ambiguous, but the selector must return a crop using the photo-center / nearest / left / upper / stable-ID fallback.

groups.title: Secondary labels and physical context
groups.description: Secondary paper, direct glass printing, a printed bottle depiction inside a carton, and a wine-glass-only negative. Nonexclusive masks preserve nested physical regions.

groups.title: Grip ownership and occluding packages
groups.description: A carton behind a hand and a legitimate body grip. Enclosure alone must not establish or reject a grip.

groups.title: Two hands: one or two subjects
groups.description: Unequal grips on different bottles remain ambiguous; two hands on one bottle support the same subject.

groups.title: Horizontal bottle versus a wine tool
groups.description: A real pouring bottle and a slender sampling tool. Tool masks are independently annotated, never renamed to fit the selector.

groups.title: Pointing, reaching and gripping
groups.description: A pointing finger touches a label versus a wrapped grip. Visible adjacency alone cannot prove a grip.

groups.title: Projected contact across depth
groups.description: A hand behind a bottle versus a physical grip. Native masks encode visible pixels, not ground-truth depth supplied to the selector.

groups.title: Real bottle inside packaging versus printed artwork
groups.description: Open gift box containing a physical bottle, and a closed carton carrying a flat bottle illustration.

groups.title: Clear gift packaging
groups.description: A window gift bag and reflective wrapping strips. Opaque native passes annotate visible physical surfaces; transparent windows are open geometry.

groups.title: Poster and mirror duplicate
groups.description: A large flat bottle poster beside a real bottle; a reflected duplicate. Physical ownership and representation masks are annotated separately. The mirror duplicate is staged virtual geometry (a reflection proxy), not a real reflected-light photo.

groups.title: Label omissions connected to the silhouette
groups.description: A missing secondary label and a missing main-label side, each connected to the exterior of the supplied detector mask. Source RGB must survive.

groups.title: Tags and paper outside the bottle body
groups.description: A hanging neck tag and a peeling paper flap. They belong to the bottle and must remain complete.

groups.title: Overlapping bottles and label owners
groups.description: Touching labels and a rear label inside the front bottle's bounding rectangle. Native owner IDs are used only for evaluation.

groups.title: Small wine information beside large signage
groups.description: A small vintage label with a large price card, and a promotional strip between bottles. Shelf signage is not a wine label.

groups.title: Photo center through an occluder
groups.description: Balanced bottles with the center covered by a foreground glass or by the bottle itself. Targets follow visible GT mask geometry, separately from intent.

groups.title: Explicit tap against hand and mask gaps
groups.description: Tap a background bottle while another is held; tap white paper missing from the predicted bottle mask. A unique tap precedes passive cues.

groups.title: Three bottles: foreground versus photo center
groups.description: Two background bottles close to center and one foreground bottle off-center. Includes overlap, edge framing, weak depth, a background magnum and an explicit background tap. Size is prominence evidence, not measured camera depth. A horizontally lying foreground bottle is a pose countercontrol.

groups.title: Bottle format versus camera distance
groups.description: Half bottles, magnums and a held small bottle. Conflicting apparent size and depth use fallback unless a grip establishes intent.

groups.title: Separate shelves and support planes
groups.description: Raised background shelves and a lying bottle on a lower level. A lower image base alone must not certify camera proximity; ambiguous scenes require the declared geometric fallback.

groups.title: Hands projected at bottle ends
groups.description: A hand behind the neck or base, contrasted with a genuine tilted pouring grip. Physical grip ownership is native evaluation metadata, never detector input.

groups.title: Real bottles crossing printed panels
groups.description: Physical foreground bottles overlap a rear printed panel. A separate controlled fault fills a panel mask across the foreground silhouette; RGB and visible GT masks remain unchanged.

groups.title: Foreground intent among crowded and occluded bottles
groups.description: Five to seven bottles, a foreground glass or a bucket and competing labels. Only visible label pixels are annotated; no hidden label content is generated.

purpose: development regression; not an unseen accuracy benchmark
masks: Native opaque visible geometry. Separate bottle, label and hand masks can overlap.
threshold_policy: semantic-v2 constants in the source commit; all changes are development tuning and must be disclosed

limitations: Paired development scenes share assets with the original native suite.
Depth, physical roles and grip ownership are evaluation annotations, never selector inputs.
Mirror identity can be inherently ambiguous from a single view; use deterministic fallback.
Mirror case uses staged virtual reflection geometry, not refraction-aware reflected-ID masks.
The pointing pose is edited developmental geometry without anatomical fit validation.
expansion.additional_controls: Two true-overlap scenes added before their detector collection; initial separated-label scenes retained as controls.

additional_coverage.interpretation: Correlated development coverage, not independent photo accuracy. Real additions are identified separately.
